analysis.investment_thesis: ACME Solar operates in India's most important energy transition sector with 2,540 MW installed and 3,780 MW under development, but five years of revenue contraction (-4.6% CAGR), a D/E of 2.72x, ROE of just 7.57%, and persistently negative free cash flow make this a leveraged infrastructure bet rather than a quality compounder. The sector story is compelling; the balance sheet is not.
key_strengths: Massive project pipeline (3,780 MW under construction) backed by government-linked PPAs offers revenue visibility once commissioned
Operating cash flow has been positive all 5 years (INR 1,543 Cr in FY25), showing project-level cash generation
Promoter holding of 83.29% signals very high promoter commitment and skin-in-the-game
key_risks: Total debt of INR 10,976 Cr with finance costs of INR 759 Cr consumes 61% of operating income — extreme leverage risk
Revenue has contracted from INR 1,777 Cr (FY20) to INR 1,405 Cr (FY25) — the existing portfolio is shrinking, not growing
Free cash flow of -INR 1,719 Cr in FY25 means the company is entirely dependent on debt markets to fund its capex pipeline
red_flags: ROE of 7.57% and ROCE of 8.42% are below my minimum hurdle rates — at this leverage, equity holders are barely compensated for the risk
Net profit of INR 698 Cr in FY24 appears inflated by other income (INR 891 Cr likely from asset monetisation) — normalised earnings power is much lower
Business is entirely dependent on central and state government-backed offtakers — a classic single-customer concentration risk I avoid
analysis.detailed_analysis: ACME Solar is an infrastructure play with a utility-scale solar portfolio, not a growth business in the traditional sense. The high operating margin (65.28%) and gross margin (99.42%) are typical of an IPP with long-term fixed-rate PPAs — but they mask the reality that finance costs devour most of that operating income. The revenue decline over 5 years reflects project decommissioning or reclassification as the company pivots to new capacity, but until the 3,780 MW pipeline is commissioned and generating revenue, the P/E of 36.8x is not supported by current earnings quality.
